name: Methenolone

card.summary: Primobolan: a mild DHT-derived steroid prized in bodybuilding for lean gains with fewer side effects; human trials exist only in anemia, cancer and rehabilitation.
card.note: One small stroke-rehabilitation RCT shows thigh-muscle gain; forum claims of mildness are not trial-tested.

quick.overview:
Methenolone (metenolone), sold as Primobolan, is an anabolic-androgenic steroid derived from dihydrotestosterone, available as an oral acetate and an injectable enanthate. In bodybuilding and looksmaxxing forums it is regarded as a mild compound for lean gains with fewer estrogenic effects.

Controlled studies are medical: a 1979 trial in refractory anemias, 1975 and later work in breast cancer, and a 2011 randomized trial in stroke patients where weekly injections increased thigh muscle area compared with controls. No study has tested it for physique or appearance in healthy people.
quick.mechanism: It is a DHT-derived androgen that binds the androgen receptor and promotes protein synthesis; Grokipedia describes the acetate form as limited by first-pass liver metabolism and the enanthate as a long-acting injectable.[1] In the stroke trial, weekly injections for six weeks increased thigh cross-sectional area.[2]
quick.risks: Trials in refractory anemia reported negligible side effects, but one randomized trial found more marked anemia and thrombocytopenia in lymphoma patients given methenolone during chemotherapy, and a rat study found worse cirrhosis-like liver changes with methenolone acetate.[3][4][5] A T Nation post reports a user's liver problems; forum users also dispute how harsh it is on lipids.[6][7] It is prohibited in sport.

lead: Methenolone (also metenolone; brand name Primobolan) is a synthetic anabolic-androgenic steroid derived from dihydrotestosterone, available as an oral acetate and an injectable enanthate ester. Grokipedia, an AI-generated encyclopedia, describes it as a relatively mild androgen introduced medically in the early 1960s for anemias and wasting.[1]

Human studies are clinical. A 19-patient trial of Primobolan in refractory anemias reported remissions in some subtypes with negligible side effects; a 1975 study of the enanthate in disseminated breast cancer reported objective remission in 8 of 41 evaluable patients and described the agent as less virilising than testosterone propionate; and a 2011 randomized trial in 26 hemiplegic stroke patients found larger thigh-muscle gains on weekly injections than in controls.[3][8][2]

In bodybuilding and looksmaxxing-adjacent communities, methenolone is discussed as a milder, lean-gain compound that some users consider less toxic than other steroids, although posters differ and no controlled study has measured its effects on appearance in healthy users.[7][9][10]
infobox: Prescription drug / controlled substance in many countries; prohibited in sport
One small RCT of muscle area in stroke patients

paras: A 1979 trial treated 19 consecutive patients with refractory anemias using methenolone; remission frequencies were 3 of 6 in pancytopenia, 2 of 4 in bicytopenia, 1 of 5 in refractory anemia with hyperplastic marrow and 1 of 4 in myelofibrosis, with no obvious prolongation of survival among responders and negligible side effects.[3] A case report described a patient with thymoma-associated pure red cell aplasia treated with cyclosporine and Primobolan who remained transfusion-dependent.[11]

In 1975 investigators treated 43 patients with disseminated breast carcinoma using metenolone enanthate at weekly doses; objective remissions longer than three months occurred in 8 of 41 evaluable patients, soft-tissue metastases responded best, and the authors judged its efficacy comparable to testosterone propionate but less virilising.[8] In 1977 a randomized trial in lymphoma found that adding high-dose metenolone during MOPP chemotherapy increased rather than reduced hematological toxicity.[4]

In forums, users describe methenolone as a lean-gain compound used on its own in TRT contexts or alongside testosterone and nandrolone.[12][13] A T Nation poster said his wife gained roughly ten pounds of muscle in four weeks on metenolone but stopped after liver issues, an anecdote with no controlled data.[6] Others say compounds that make users look big, such as nandrolone or methandienone, are no better at building muscle than Winstrol, Primobolan or Masteron.[9]

Clinical studies include a 19-patient trial in refractory anemias, a 1975 breast-cancer study of the enanthate, a 1977 randomized trial in lymphoma during chemotherapy and a 2011 randomized trial of 26 stroke patients showing larger thigh-muscle gains on weekly injections.[3][8][4][2] There are no trials in healthy people for appearance.

In a randomized trial of 26 subacute stroke patients, weekly injections of metenolone enanthate for six weeks increased thigh cross-sectional area on CT by 13.4 percent on the affected side and 14.5 percent on the unaffected side, versus 3.3 and 5.2 percent in controls, without specific training; the authors concluded it was effective for improving muscle area in stroke rehabilitation.[2] A related study examined anabolic steroid administration combined with passive muscle stretching on expression of a muscle growth factor.[14] No trial has tested methenolone for bodybuilding or appearance in healthy people.

The refractory-anemia trial reported negligible side effects, whereas the lymphoma trial reported more marked anemia and thrombocytopenia with methenolone plus chemotherapy.[3][4] In rats with thioacetamide-induced cirrhosis, methenolone acetate treatment was followed by more serious structural liver alterations than in untreated animals.[5] A rat study cited on T Nation examined cardiac effects of metenolone enanthate during puberty.[15][13]

Forum posters differ on its safety: one says it is safer than testosterone at high doses though harsher on lipids, another argues it may be less toxic acutely than testosterone at supraphysiologic doses, and a patient on T Nation says he added it to a TRT protocol for ulcerative colitis.[7][10][16]

Grokipedia describes metenolone as a DHT-derived 3-hydroxy steroid with the acetate absorbed orally and the enanthate released over 10 to 14 days after injection; no primary pharmacokinetic study was identified here.[1] A poster notes it cannot be legally compounded for human use in the US because it lacks the relevant approved active ingredient.[17]

A 1989 survey of competitive bodybuilders documented the incidence of anabolic steroid use, and a registered study (NCT07568574) plans to examine medically supervised performance-enhancing substances in elite athletes.[18][19] On T Nation, methenolone is mentioned among compounds added to TRT regimens for wellness and in lean-bulk stack discussions.[12][13]

timeline.event: Treatment of disseminated breast carcinoma with metenolone enanthate is reported.[8]
A randomized trial finds more hematological toxicity with metenolone during lymphoma chemotherapy.[4]
A trial of methenolone in refractory anemias is published.[3]
A randomized trial reports thigh-muscle gains in stroke patients given metenolone enanthate.[2]

lore.intro: Primobolan is discussed on T Nation as a mild compound for lean gains, with claims about lower toxicity and disagreement over its effect on lipids.[7][10][9]

claims.claim: Primobolan is a milder, safer steroid.
claims.believers: Posters say it may be less toxic than testosterone at high doses, or that it is safer than most anabolics.[7][10]
claims.experts: A trial in refractory anemia reported negligible side effects, but a lymphoma trial reported increased hematological toxicity and a rat study reported worse liver changes.[3][4][5]

claims.believers: A forum poster reported a user gaining ten pounds of muscle in four weeks; another says it is no better than other lean compounds.[6][9]
claims.experts: A randomized trial in stroke patients found greater thigh muscle area with weekly injections; no study in healthy users exists.[2]

claims.believers: One poster says its lipid effects make it less safe than testosterone, though safer than others.[7]
claims.experts: No lipid trial of methenolone was located.
